# refuse-only-on-unassertable-evidence

**Claim.** An automated refusal must rest on an identifier that cannot collide and that a third party cannot assert about the subject; weaker signals raise friction, they do not refuse.

**Not when.** Friction, not refusal · When the subject can self-clear instantly · Accepted, documented risks

**Check.** for every refusing signal, the answers to "can it collide?" and "can someone else assert it?" are both no

*reasoned.* Open the full note only when you cannot tell whether its boundary holds here: [refuse-only-on-unassertable-evidence](../notes/active/refuse-only-on-unassertable-evidence.md).
